body:
[aida:advisor] LANE STOPPED. BUG-1442 no-op'd in a fourth way and wrote a false Done.

I told you: "if a member no-ops despite the realignment, that assumption is wrong and I
stop the lane." It did. I am holding to that.

WHAT HAPPENED ON BUG-1442 — not divergence, not a fork, a SWAP.

  dispatched  BUG-1442, PR #2027, branch bug-1442-work at 6c692a496b
  the implementer swapped mid-phase to bug-1485-work and pushed to PR #2030
  the drain marked BUG-1442 DONE on the strength of "PR-2030 opened"
  three lines later it printed: "the PR credits BUG-1485 - crediting BUG-1485,
   BUG-1442 stays queued"

Nothing undid the Done. PR #2030 is BUG-1485's, orchestrator lease-matching. BUG-1442
is a TOON rendering defect. Unrelated specs, and BUG-1442 has an outstanding
RequestChanges verdict — so it sat reading work-finished-awaiting-merge with its
findings unaddressed and its own head untouched.

The drain had the credit fact and wrote the status anyway, then printed the fact.

Filed BUG-1527, high, drive. Status corrected by hand.

THIS BREAKS THE GUARD ARGUMENT WE BOTH MADE. BUG-1522's guard does not catch it. A PR
did open and a head did move — just not the dispatched spec's. Any check asking "did a
head move" rather than "did THIS branch move" passes it clean.

So it is FOUR, not three:

  BUG-1524  drain continues after phase 1 refuses to launch    no implementer ran
  BUG-1522  no-op guard unreachable on the paths taken         nothing notices
  BUG-1525  brief generator forks a fresh lineage              brief lane only
  BUG-1527  implementer ran on the WRONG SPEC, dispatched spec closed on its PR

NOT ESTABLISHED: why the swap happened. A vendor error appears immediately before it —
"codex_models_manager: failed to refresh available models: timeout waiting for child
process to exit" — and I do not know if it is causal. BUG-1527 asserts only that the
drain accepted the swap.

REVISED POSITION, and it reverses what I told you an hour ago. I argued the lane should
continue because the trigger was measured gone. That was true of the trigger I knew
about, and I generalised from one cleared condition to the lane being safe. Two members
in, the second failed a way I had not enumerated, and this one is worse than a stall
because it writes a lie into the substrate rather than merely wasting a cycle.

The twelve remaining stay undispatched until BUG-1527 and BUG-1522 are in. I would put
BUG-1527 first of those two: BUG-1522 makes a silent failure loud, but BUG-1527 is the
one currently capable of closing a spec on another spec's work.

SEPARATELY — the reviewer's PR-2034 verdict landed: REQUEST-CHANGES, Build RED. Not a
stale base; they ran the control (main alone passes, merged tree fails). Cause is the
prose-classifier inventory embedding LINE NUMBERS — the PR added 51 lines above three
marked sites, zero classifier markers changed. That step is 12 of 25 under bash -e, so
it skipped thirteen steps including Run tests. The regression test this whole round
exists to add has never executed.

Filed by them as BUG-1526; I approved it HIGH as a throughput blocker, because any PR
adding lines above lib.rs:36992 trips it regardless of what it touches.

ONE MORE THING WORTH YOUR ATTENTION: BUG-1485 now has real work on PR #2030 that was
produced by a drain dispatched for a different spec. The work looks legitimate and I am
not discarding it, but nobody dispatched it and no brief asked for it. If you are
tracking what is in flight, PR #2030 is in flight without anyone having decided it
should be.
subject: LANE STOPPED: BUG-1442 no-op'd a fourth way — false Done written on another spec's PR (BUG-1527); reversing my continue-the-lane call
